chapters.title: Solomon Asks for Wisdom
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 1

At Gibeon

1Solomon son of David established himself firmly over his kingdom, and the LORD his God was with him and made him exceedingly great.

2Solomon spoke to all Israel, to the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, to the judges and to every leader in all Israel, the heads of the fathers' houses.

3Then Solomon and all the assembly with him went to the high place at Gibeon, for the tent of meeting of God was there, which Moses the servant of the LORD had made in the wilderness.

4But David had brought up the ark of God from Kiriath-jearim to the place David had prepared for it, for he had pitched a tent for it in Jerusalem.

5The bronze altar that Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, had made was there before the dwelling of the LORD, and Solomon and the assembly sought Him there.

6Solomon went up there to the bronze altar before the LORD, which was at the tent of meeting, and offered a thousand burnt offerings on it.

7That night God appeared to Solomon and said to him, "Ask what I shall give you."

8Solomon said to God, "You have shown great loyal love to David my father, and have made me king in his place.

9Now, LORD God, let Your word to David my father be confirmed, for You have made me king over a people as many as the dust of the earth.

10Now give me wisdom and knowledge, so that I may go out and come in before this people, for who can judge this great people of Yours?"

11God said to Solomon, "Because this was in your heart, and you have not asked for riches, wealth or honor, or the life of those who hate you, and have not even asked for long life, but have asked for wisdom and knowledge for yourself, so that you may judge My people over whom I have made you king,

12wisdom and knowledge are granted to you. I will also give you riches, wealth and honor such as none of the kings before you had, and none after you will have."

13So Solomon came from the high place at Gibeon, from before the tent of meeting, to Jerusalem, and he reigned over Israel.

Horses and Chariots

14Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen. He had one thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, and he stationed them in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.

15The king made silver and gold as common in Jerusalem as stones, and he made cedars as plentiful as the sycamore trees of the lowland.

16Solomon's horses were brought out of Egypt and from Kue; the king's traders bought them from Kue at a price.

17They brought up a chariot from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver and a horse for a hundred and fifty, and so they brought them out by their hand for all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Aram.

Notes

  • v3 "the high place at Gibeon, for the tent of meeting of God was there" — Kings says only that Solomon went to Gibeon for that was the great high place (1 Kings 3:4). Chronicles gives the reason a high place was lawful: the tent Moses made and its altar stood there (1 Chronicles 16:39; 21:29), while the ark was in a tent in Jerusalem (v4).

  • v5 "The bronze altar that Bezalel… had made… sought Him there" — the altar of Exodus 38:1, made by Bezalel son of Uri son of Hur (Exodus 31:2). Va-yidreshehu can be sought Him, the LORD, or sought it, the altar; the Greek has it. Seek the LORD is this book's word for faithfulness (1 Chronicles 22:19; 28:9).

  • v7 "That night God appeared to Solomon" — Kings has in a dream by night (1 Kings 3:5); Chronicles does not mention a dream.

  • vv9–10 "as many as the dust of the earth… go out and come in before this people" — the promise to Abraham, I will make your seed like the dust of the earth (Genesis 13:16), now a people to be judged. Go out and come in before them is what Moses asked for in a successor, so that the congregation of the LORD may not be like sheep that have no shepherd (Numbers 27:17).

  • v10 "wisdom and knowledge" — chokhmah u-madda. In Kings Solomon asks for a listening heart, lev shome'a (1 Kings 3:9). Madda, knowledge, is found again only in Daniel 1:4, 17 and Ecclesiastes 10:20.

  • v13 "from the high place at Gibeon" — the Hebrew has la-bamah, to the high place, which cannot stand with from before the tent of meeting… to Jerusalem. The Greek has ek, from. The text follows the Greek.

  • vv14–17 horses from Egypt — the law of the king: he shall not multiply horses for himself, nor make the people return to Egypt in order to multiply horses (Deuteronomy 17:16). Chronicles sets the horse trade right after the gift of wisdom and riches; Kings tells it at the height of his glory (1 Kings 10:26–29).

  • v15 "silver and gold as common… as stones" — Kings has silver alone (1 Kings 10:27); Chronicles adds gold.

chapters.title: Solomon and Hiram
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 2

Solomon's Letter

1Solomon gave orders to build a house for the name of the LORD and a house for his kingdom.

2Solomon counted out seventy thousand men to carry loads, eighty thousand to cut stone in the hill country, and three thousand six hundred to oversee them.

3Solomon sent to Hiram king of Tyre, saying, "As you dealt with David my father, and sent him cedars to build himself a house to live in —

4I am about to build a house for the name of the LORD my God, to dedicate it to Him, to burn fragrant incense before Him, for the bread set out continually, and for burnt offerings morning and evening, on the sabbaths, the new moons and the appointed feasts of the LORD our God, as Israel must do forever.

5The house I am building will be great, for our God is greater than all gods.

6But who is able to build Him a house, since heaven, even the highest heaven, cannot contain Him? Who am I, that I should build Him a house, except as a place to burn incense before Him?

7So now send me a man skilled to work in gold, silver, bronze and iron, and in purple, crimson and blue, who knows how to engrave, to work with the skilled men who are with me in Judah and Jerusalem, whom David my father provided.

8Send me also cedar, cypress and algum timber from Lebanon, for I know that your servants know how to cut the timber of Lebanon. My servants will be with your servants

9to prepare timber for me in abundance, for the house I am building will be great and wonderful.

10For your servants, the woodcutters who fell the trees, I will give twenty thousand cors of crushed wheat, twenty thousand cors of barley, twenty thousand baths of wine and twenty thousand baths of oil."

Hiram's Answer

11Hiram king of Tyre answered in a letter that he sent to Solomon: "Because the LORD loves His people, He has made you king over them."

12Hiram said, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who made heaven and earth, who has given King David a wise son, endowed with insight and understanding, who will build a house for the LORD and a house for his kingdom.

13Now I am sending a skilled man, endowed with understanding, Huram-abi,

14the son of a woman of the daughters of Dan, and his father was a man of Tyre. He knows how to work in gold, silver, bronze and iron, in stone and wood, in purple, blue, fine linen and crimson, and to do every kind of engraving and carry out any design that is given him, with your skilled men and the skilled men of my lord David your father.

15Now let my lord send his servants the wheat and barley, the oil and wine, of which he has spoken.

16We will cut whatever timber you need from Lebanon and bring it to you as rafts by sea to Joppa, and you will take it up to Jerusalem."

The Guests at Work

17Solomon counted all the guests who were in the land of Israel, after the census that David his father had taken of them, and they were found to be a hundred and fifty-three thousand six hundred.

18He made seventy thousand of them carry loads, eighty thousand cut stone in the hill country, and three thousand six hundred oversee the people at work.

Notes

  • v1 the numbering — in the Hebrew this verse is 1:18, and vv2–18 are 2:1–17. The text follows the English numbering.

  • v3 "As you dealt with David my father… —" — the sentence has no second half: as you did… [so do with me]. The Greek leaves it unfinished too. In Kings the letter begins differently, with why David could not build (1 Kings 5:3).

  • v3 "Hiram" — the Hebrew of Chronicles writes Churam, Huram, here and through the book; Kings writes Chiram, Hiram (1 Kings 5:1). The Greek has Cheiram in both books. He is the same king.

  • v6 "heaven, even the highest heaven, cannot contain Him" — ha-shamayim u-shemei ha-shamayim lo yekhalkeluhu, the words of Solomon's prayer at the dedication, The heavens, even the highest heavens, cannot contain You (1 Kings 8:27). Here he says it before a stone is laid.

  • v10 "crushed wheat" — chittim makkot, beaten wheat. Kings has chittim makkolet, wheat as food (1 Kings 5:11); the two words differ by one letter.

  • v11 "Because the LORD loves His people" — the reason the queen of Sheba gives: Because the LORD loved Israel forever, He has made you king (1 Kings 10:9). Here a king of Tyre says it first.

  • v12 "the God of Israel, who made heaven and earth" — in Kings Hiram says only Blessed be the LORD today (1 Kings 5:7). In Chronicles the foreign king names the LORD as maker of heaven and earth.

  • vv13–14 "Huram-abi, the son of a woman of the daughters of Dan" — le-Churam avi, Huram my father, father as a title, as Joseph was a father to Pharaoh (Genesis 45:8). Kings calls him Hiram, the son of a widow of the tribe of Naphtali (1 Kings 7:14). Of the daughters of Dan: Bezalel built the tabernacle with Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan (Exodus 31:6), and the house has a man of Dan at the work again.

  • vv17–18 "all the guests who were in the land of Israel" — ha-gerim, the men David had gathered to cut the stone (1 Chronicles 22:2). The three numbers are those of v2: the workforce is the guests.

chapters.title: The Building of the House
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 3

The Site and the Measures

1Solomon began to build the house of the LORD in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where the LORD had appeared to David his father, at the place that David had prepared, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

2He began to build in the second month, on the second day, in the fourth year of his reign.

3These are the foundations Solomon laid for building the house of God: the length, in cubits of the old standard, was sixty cubits, and the width twenty cubits.

4The porch in front, across the width of the house, was twenty cubits long, and its height was a hundred and twenty. He overlaid it inside with pure gold.

The Great House

5He paneled the great house with cypress wood, overlaid it with fine gold, and worked palm trees and chains on it.

6He adorned the house with precious stones for beauty, and the gold was gold of Parvaim.

7He overlaid the house with gold, its beams, its thresholds, its walls and its doors, and he engraved cherubim on the walls.

The Most Holy Place

8He made the room of the Most Holy Place. Its length, across the width of the house, was twenty cubits, and its width twenty cubits. He overlaid it with fine gold, six hundred talents.

9The weight of the nails was fifty shekels of gold. He overlaid the upper rooms with gold.

10In the room of the Most Holy Place he made two cherubim of sculptured work, and they overlaid them with gold.

11The wings of the cherubim were twenty cubits long. One wing of the one, five cubits, touched the wall of the house, and its other wing, five cubits, touched the wing of the other cherub.

12One wing of the other cherub, five cubits, touched the wall of the house, and its other wing, five cubits, met the wing of the first cherub.

13The wings of these cherubim spread out twenty cubits. They stood on their feet, and their faces were toward the house.

14He made the veil of blue, purple, crimson and fine linen, and worked cherubim on it.

The Pillars

15In front of the house he made two pillars, thirty-five cubits high, and the capital on the top of each was five cubits.

16He made chains, in the inner sanctuary, and put them on the tops of the pillars, and he made a hundred pomegranates and put them on the chains.

17He set up the pillars in front of the nave, one on the right and one on the left. He called the one on the right Jachin and the one on the left Boaz.

Notes

  • v1 "on Mount Moriah, where the LORD had appeared to David" — the name is found elsewhere only in Genesis 22:2, the land of Moriah, where Abraham was sent to offer Isaac. There the place was named for seeing: On the mountain of the LORD it will be seen (Genesis 22:14). Here, nir'ah, He appeared, from the same verb: at Ornan's threshing floor David saw the messenger of the LORD, and the LORD answered him with fire (1 Chronicles 21:16, 26).

  • v3 "cubits of the old standard" — ba-middah ha-rishonah, by the first measure, an older standard than the writer's own. Ezekiel's measuring cubit is a cubit and a handbreadth (Ezekiel 40:5). The measures, sixty by twenty, are those of Kings (1 Kings 6:2).

  • v4 "its height was a hundred and twenty" — the house itself was thirty cubits high (1 Kings 6:2); Kings gives the porch no height (1 Kings 6:3). The Greek also has a hundred and twenty. The text keeps the number.

  • v6 "gold of Parvaim" — a place named only here. Where it was is not known.

  • v10 "cherubim of sculptured work" — ma'aseh tsa'tsu'im, a word found only here, of uncertain meaning. The Greek has a work of wood, as Kings has the cherubim made of olivewood (1 Kings 6:23).

  • v13 "their faces were toward the house" — the cherubim of the tabernacle faced one toward the other… toward the cover (Exodus 25:20). These stand on their feet and face the house.

  • v14 "the veil of blue, purple, crimson and fine linen… cherubim on it" — the veil of the tabernacle, of blue and purple and crimson and fine twisted linen… with cherubim (Exodus 26:31). Kings has doors of olivewood at the entrance of the inner sanctuary (1 Kings 6:31) and no veil.

  • v15 "two pillars, thirty-five cubits high" — Kings has eighteen cubits (1 Kings 7:15). The text keeps the Hebrew of each.

  • v16 "chains, in the inner sanctuary" — ba-devir, which does not fit pillars standing at the porch; the Greek copies the word, en tō dabeir. The text keeps the Hebrew.

  • v17 "Jachin… Boaz" — Yakhin, from kun, to establish, the verb of the promise to David, I will establish his throne forever (1 Chronicles 17:12). Boaz is the name of David's great-grandfather (Ruth 4:21).

chapters.title: The Furnishings of the House
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 4

The Altar, the Sea and the Basins

1He made an altar of bronze, twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide and ten cubits high.

2He made the sea of cast metal. It was round, ten cubits from brim to brim and five cubits high, and a line of thirty cubits measured its circumference.

3Under it, all around, were figures of oxen encircling it, ten to a cubit, going around the sea. The oxen were in two rows, cast with it when it was cast.

4It stood on twelve oxen, three facing north, three facing west, three facing south and three facing east. The sea was set on them, and all their hindquarters were toward the inside.

5Its thickness was a handbreadth, and its brim was made like the brim of a cup, like a lily blossom. It held three thousand baths.

6He made ten basins, and set five on the right and five on the left, for washing. In them they rinsed what was used for the burnt offering, and the sea was for the priests to wash in.

The Lampstands, Tables and Courts

7He made ten lampstands of gold as prescribed for them, and set them in the nave, five on the right and five on the left.

8He made ten tables and placed them in the nave, five on the right and five on the left. He made a hundred bowls of gold.

9He made the court of the priests and the great court, and doors for the court, and overlaid their doors with bronze.

10He set the sea on the right side, to the southeast.

Huram's Work

11Huram made the pots, the shovels and the bowls. So Huram finished the work that he did for King Solomon in the house of God:

12the two pillars, the bowls and the capitals on the tops of the pillars, and the two networks to cover the two bowls of the capitals on the tops of the pillars;

13the four hundred pomegranates for the two networks, two rows of pomegranates for each network, to cover the two bowls of the capitals on the pillars;

14the stands, and the basins on the stands;

15the one sea, and the twelve oxen under it;

16the pots, the shovels, the forks and all their utensils. Huram-abi made them for King Solomon for the house of the LORD, of burnished bronze.

17In the plain of the Jordan the king cast them, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zeredah.

18Solomon made all these utensils in great abundance, for the weight of the bronze could not be found out.

The Gold Furnishings

19Solomon made all the furnishings that were in the house of God: the golden altar, the tables with the bread of the Presence on them,

20the lampstands and their lamps of pure gold, to burn before the inner sanctuary as prescribed;

21the flowers, the lamps and the tongs, of gold, of the purest gold;

22the snuffers, the bowls, the dishes for incense and the fire pans, of pure gold; and the entrance of the house, its inner doors to the Most Holy Place and the doors of the house to the nave, of gold.

Notes

  • v1 "an altar of bronze, twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide and ten cubits high" — Kings names the bronze altar (1 Kings 8:64) but gives no measures. The altar of the tabernacle was five cubits long and five cubits wide… and three cubits its height (Exodus 27:1).

  • v3 "figures of oxen" — demut beqarim. Kings has peqa'im, gourds, in the same sentence (1 Kings 7:24). The two Hebrew words differ in two letters; the Greek of Chronicles has calves. The text keeps the Hebrew of each.

  • v5 "It held three thousand baths" — Kings has two thousand baths (1 Kings 7:26). The text keeps the Hebrew of each.

  • v6 "the sea was for the priests to wash in" — Kings does not give its use. Chronicles gives it the work of the bronze basin of the tabernacle, from which Aaron and his sons shall wash their hands and their feet (Exodus 30:18–19).

  • vv7–8 "ten lampstands… ten tables" — the tabernacle had one lampstand and one table (Exodus 25:23, 31). Kings has ten lampstands (1 Kings 7:49); Chronicles has ten of each.

  • vv11, 16 "Huram… Huram-abi" — in v11 the name is written Chiram, Hiram, and read Churam, Huram; the text follows the read form. In v16 he is Churam aviv, Huram his father, the title of 2:13.

  • v17 "between Succoth and Zeredah" — Kings has Zarethan (1 Kings 7:46).

  • v18 "the weight of the bronze could not be found out" — lo nechqar, was not searched out, as David had said: bronze and iron beyond weighing, for there is so much of it (1 Chronicles 22:14).

chapters.title: The Ark Brought into the House
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 5

The Ark Brought Up

1So all the work that Solomon did for the house of the LORD was finished. Solomon brought in the things David his father had dedicated, the silver, the gold and all the vessels, and put them in the treasuries of the house of God.

2Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel and all the heads of the tribes, the leaders of the fathers' houses of the sons of Israel, in Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD from the City of David, which is Zion.

3All the men of Israel assembled before the king at the feast, which is in the seventh month.

chapters.title: Solomon's Prayer of Dedication
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 6

Solomon Blesses the Assembly

1Then Solomon said,
"The LORD has said that He would dwell in thick darkness.

2I have built You an exalted house,
a place for You to dwell in forever."

3Then the king turned his face and blessed all the assembly of Israel, while all the assembly of Israel stood.

4He said, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who spoke with His mouth to David my father, and with His hands has fulfilled it, saying,

5'Since the day that I brought My people out of the land of Egypt, I have not chosen a city out of all the tribes of Israel in which to build a house, so that My name might be there, and I have not chosen a man to be leader over My people Israel.

6But I have chosen Jerusalem, that My name might be there, and I have chosen David to be over My people Israel.'

7It was in the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.

8But the LORD said to David my father, 'Because it was in your heart to build a house for My name, you did well that it was in your heart.

9Only, you shall not build the house, but your son who shall come from your body, he shall build the house for My name.'

10Now the LORD has fulfilled His word that He spoke: I have risen in place of David my father, and I sit on the throne of Israel, as the LORD promised, and I have built the house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.

11There I have put the ark, in which is the covenant of the LORD that He made with the sons of Israel."

The Prayer

12Then he stood before the altar of the LORD in the presence of all the assembly of Israel, and spread out his hands.

13For Solomon had made a bronze platform, five cubits long, five cubits wide and three cubits high, and had set it in the middle of the court. He stood on it, knelt on his knees in the presence of all the assembly of Israel, and spread out his hands toward the heavens,

14and said, "O LORD, God of Israel, there is no God like You in the heavens or on the earth, keeping covenant and loyal love with Your servants who walk before You with all their heart,

15who have kept with Your servant David my father what You promised him. You spoke with Your mouth, and with Your hand You have fulfilled it this day.

16And now, O LORD, God of Israel, keep with Your servant David my father what You promised him, saying, 'You shall not lack a man before Me to sit on the throne of Israel, if only your sons take heed to their way, to walk in My instruction as you have walked before Me.'

17And now, O LORD, God of Israel, let Your word be confirmed, which You spoke to Your servant David.

18But will God indeed dwell with man on the earth? The heavens, even the highest heavens, cannot contain You; how much less this house that I have built!

19Yet turn toward the prayer of Your servant and his plea, O LORD my God, to listen to the cry and the prayer that Your servant prays before You,

20that Your eyes may be open toward this house day and night, toward the place where You have said You would put Your name, to listen to the prayer that Your servant prays toward this place.

21Listen to the pleas of Your servant and of Your people Israel when they pray toward this place. Hear from the place of Your dwelling, from the heavens; hear and forgive.

22If a man sins against his neighbor and is made to take an oath, and comes and swears his oath before Your altar in this house,

23then hear from the heavens and act, and judge Your servants, repaying the guilty by bringing his conduct on his own head, and vindicating the righteous by rewarding him according to his righteousness.

24When Your people Israel are struck down before an enemy because they have sinned against You, and they turn back and confess Your name and pray and plead before You in this house,

25then hear from the heavens and forgive the sin of Your people Israel, and bring them back to the land that You gave to them and to their fathers.

26When the heavens are shut up and there is no rain because they have sinned against You, and they pray toward this place and confess Your name and turn from their sin because You afflict them,

27then hear in the heavens and forgive the sin of Your servants, Your people Israel, when You teach them the good way in which they should walk, and give rain on Your land that You have given to Your people as an inheritance.

28If there is famine in the land, if there is plague, scorching or mildew, locust or grasshopper, if their enemies besiege them in the land of their gates, whatever blow, whatever sickness there is,

29whatever prayer, whatever plea is made by any man or by all Your people Israel, each knowing his own blow and his own pain, and spreading out his hands toward this house,

30then hear from the heavens, the place of Your dwelling, and forgive, and give to each man according to all his ways, whose heart You know — for You, You alone, know the hearts of the sons of men —

31so that they may fear You and walk in Your ways all the days that they live on the face of the land that You gave to our fathers.

32Also concerning the foreigner, who is not of Your people Israel, but comes from a far country for the sake of Your great name and Your mighty hand and Your outstretched arm, when they come and pray toward this house,

33hear from the heavens, the place of Your dwelling, and do according to all that the foreigner calls to You for, so that all the peoples of the earth may know Your name and fear You, as do Your people Israel, and may know that this house that I have built is called by Your name.

34When Your people go out to battle against their enemies, by whatever way You send them, and they pray to You toward this city that You have chosen and the house that I have built for Your name,

35then hear from the heavens their prayer and their plea, and uphold their cause.

36When they sin against You — for there is no man who does not sin — and You are angry with them and give them to an enemy, so that their captors carry them away captive to a land far off or near,

37yet if they take it to heart in the land to which they have been carried captive, and turn back and plead with You in the land of their captivity, saying, 'We have sinned, we have done wrong and acted wickedly,'

38and if they turn back to You with all their heart and with all their soul in the land of their captivity, to which they were carried captive, and pray toward their land, which You gave to their fathers, and the city that You have chosen and the house that I have built for Your name,

39then hear from the heavens, the place of Your dwelling, their prayer and their pleas, and uphold their cause, and forgive Your people who have sinned against You.

40Now, my God, let Your eyes be open and Your ears attentive to the prayer made in this place.

41So now arise, O LORD God, to Your resting place,
You and the ark of Your strength.
Let Your priests, O LORD God, be clothed with salvation,
and let Your loyal ones rejoice in what is good.

42O LORD God, do not turn away the face of Your anointed ones.
Remember the loyal love shown to David Your servant."

Notes

  • vv1–42 and 1 Kings 8:12–50 — the same prayer, with changes noted below. Chronicles ends differently: Kings goes on to the iron furnace and Moses (1 Kings 8:51–53); Chronicles closes with a psalm (vv41–42).

  • vv1–2 "He would dwell in thick darkness" — ba-arafel, the darkness Moses entered on Sinai: Moses drew near to the thick darkness where God was (Exodus 20:21).

  • vv5–6 "and I have not chosen a man to be leader… But I have chosen Jerusalem" — Kings has neither clause (1 Kings 8:16). In Chronicles the two choosings stand side by side, a city and a man, as they do in the promise of 1 Chronicles 17.

  • v13 "a bronze platform, five cubits long, five cubits wide and three cubits high" — not in Kings. The word is kiyyor, elsewhere a basin (4:6), here something he stands and kneels on. Its measures are those of the altar of the tabernacle, five cubits long and five cubits wide… and three cubits its height (Exodus 27:1).

  • v16 "to walk in My instruction as you have walked before Me" — la-lekhet be-torati. Kings has to walk before Me (1 Kings 8:25). Chronicles names the torah as the way of walking before Him.

  • v18 "will God indeed dwell with man on the earth?" — et ha-adam, with humankind, is not in Kings (1 Kings 8:27). The question is now whether God lives among people.

  • v29 "each knowing his own blow and his own pain" — nig'o u-makh'ovo. Kings has the blow of his own heart (1 Kings 8:38).

  • vv41–42 "arise, O LORD God, to Your resting place, You and the ark of Your strength" — Psalm 132:8–10, with changes: the psalm's priests are clothed with righteousness (tsedeq), these with salvation (teshu'ah); the psalm's anointed one is singular, here plural, meshichekha, Your anointed ones. The Greek reads do not turn away Your face, with no anointed.

  • v42 "Remember the loyal love shown to David" — chasdei David, the loyal loves of David, which can be read two ways. (a) The LORD's loyal love promised to David, as in Isaiah 55:3, an everlasting covenant, the loyal love shown to David, which is sure: the prayer that began by asking God to keep His word to David (v16) ends by asking Him to remember it. (b) David's own deeds of loyal love, the sense the same noun has for Hezekiah's deeds, va-chasadav (32:32), and Josiah's (35:26): remember what David did for the house. The text uses (a).

chapters.title: Fire from Heaven and the LORD's Answer
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 7

The Fire and the Glory

1When Solomon had finished praying, fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices, and the glory of the LORD filled the house.

2The priests could not enter the house of the LORD, because the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD.

3All the sons of Israel saw the fire come down and the glory of the LORD on the house, and they bowed with their faces to the ground on the pavement. They bowed down and gave thanks to the LORD, "For He is good, for His loyal love endures forever."

The Dedication

4Then the king and all the people offered sacrifice before the LORD.

5King Solomon offered a sacrifice of twenty-two thousand oxen and a hundred and twenty thousand sheep. So the king and all the people dedicated the house of God.

6The priests stood at their posts, and the Levites with the instruments for the song of the LORD that King David had made to give thanks to the LORD, "for His loyal love endures forever," when David offered praise by their hands. Opposite them the priests sounded trumpets, and all Israel stood.

7Solomon consecrated the middle of the court that was in front of the house of the LORD, for there he offered the burnt offerings and the fat of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar Solomon had made could not hold the burnt offering, the grain offering and the fat.

8So Solomon held the feast at that time for seven days, and all Israel with him, a very great assembly, from Lebo-hamath to the Brook of Egypt.

9On the eighth day they held a closing assembly, for they had kept the dedication of the altar seven days and the feast seven days.

10On the twenty-third day of the seventh month he sent the people away to their tents, joyful and glad of heart for the good the LORD had done for David, for Solomon and for Israel His people.

11So Solomon finished the house of the LORD and the king's house. All that Solomon had set his heart to do in the house of the LORD and in his own house, he carried out with success.

The LORD Appears to Solomon

12The LORD appeared to Solomon by night and said to him, "I have heard your prayer and have chosen this place for Myself as a house of sacrifice.

13If I shut up the heavens so that there is no rain, or if I command the grasshopper to devour the land, or if I send plague among My people,

14and My people who are called by My name humble themselves, and pray and seek My face and turn from their evil ways, then I will hear from heaven, and forgive their sin and heal their land.

15Now My eyes will be open and My ears attentive to the prayer made in this place.

16I have chosen and consecrated this house, so that My name may be there forever. My eyes and My heart will be there for all time.

17As for you, if you walk before Me as David your father walked, doing all that I have commanded you, and keep My statutes and My rules,

18then I will establish the throne of your kingdom, as I covenanted with David your father, saying, 'You shall not lack a man to rule in Israel.'

19But if you turn away and forsake My statutes and My commandments that I have set before you, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them,

20then I will uproot them from My land that I have given them, and this house that I have consecrated for My name I will cast out of My sight, and I will make it a proverb and a byword among all the peoples.

21As for this house, which was exalted, everyone who passes by it will be appalled and will say, 'Why has the LORD done this to this land and to this house?'

22Then they will say, 'Because they forsook the LORD, the God of their fathers, who brought them out of the land of Egypt, and took hold of other gods and bowed down to them and served them. That is why He has brought all this evil on them.'"

Notes

  • vv1–3 "fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offering" — not in Kings. As at the first offering of the tabernacle: Fire came out from before the LORD and consumed the burnt offering… All the people saw, and they shouted, and they fell on their faces (Leviticus 9:24); and as David was answered with fire from heaven on the same ground (1 Chronicles 21:26). The people's answer is the singers' refrain, For He is good, for His loyal love endures forever (5:13).

  • v6 "when David offered praise by their hands" — be-hallel David be-yadam: the Levites play David's instruments, and the praise is counted as his.

  • vv8–10 "seven days… the eighth day… the twenty-third day" — Kings has seven days and seven days, fourteen days, and sends the people home on the eighth day (1 Kings 8:65–66). Chronicles explains the fourteen: the dedication of the altar, then the feast, then a closing assembly, atseret, the eighth day of Booths (Leviticus 23:36).

  • v12 "a house of sacrifice" — beit zavach, a phrase found only here.

  • vv13–15 "If I shut up the heavens… and My people… humble themselves… I will hear from heaven" — not in Kings. The LORD answers the prayer in its own words: the heavens are shut up and there is no rain (6:26), plague (6:28), hear from the heavens and forgive (6:21). V15 answers 6:40 word for word. The insect differs: the prayer names arbeh and chasil (6:28), the answer chagav, grasshopper, the word of Leviticus 11:22 and Numbers 13:33.

  • v14 "humble themselves" — yikkane'u, the word on which Chronicles weighs its kings: Rehoboam's officials humbled themselves (12:6–7), and Hezekiah (32:26), Manasseh (33:12) and Josiah (34:27); Amon did not humble himself (33:23), nor did Zedekiah (36:12).

  • v18 "as I covenanted with David… a man to rule in Israel" — Kings has as I promised and a man on the throne of Israel (1 Kings 9:5). Karatti, I cut a covenant, and moshel be-Yisrael, one who rules in Israel, the words of Micah 5:2, from you shall come out for Me one who is to rule in Israel.

  • v20 "I will uproot them from My land" — u-netashtim, the verb of the curse in Deuteronomy, The LORD uprooted them from their ground (Deuteronomy 29:28). Kings has I will cut off Israel (1 Kings 9:7).

As for this house, which was exalted, everyone who passes by it will be appalled and will say, 'Why has the LORD done this to this land and to this house?'

Then they will say, 'Because they forsook the LORD, the God of their fathers, who brought them out of the land of Egypt, and took hold of other gods and bowed down to them and served them. That is why He has brought all this evil on them.'"

chapters.title: Solomon's Cities and Service
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 8

Solomon's Building

1And it came to pass at the end of twenty years, in which Solomon had built the house of the LORD and his own house,

2that Solomon rebuilt the cities that Hiram had given him, and settled the sons of Israel there.

3Solomon went to Hamath-zobah and took it.

4He built Tadmor in the wilderness, and all the store cities that he built in Hamath.

5He built Upper Beth-horon and Lower Beth-horon, fortified cities with walls, gates and bars,

6and Baalath, and all the store cities that Solomon had, all the cities for his chariots and the cities for his horsemen, and whatever Solomon desired to build in Jerusalem, in Lebanon and in all the land of his dominion.

The Forced Labor

7All the people who were left of the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites, who were not of Israel —

8their sons who were left after them in the land, whom the sons of Israel had not destroyed — these Solomon raised as forced labor, to this day.

9But of the sons of Israel Solomon made no slaves for his work. They were men of war, commanders of his officers, and commanders of his chariots and his horsemen.

10These were the chief officers of King Solomon, two hundred and fifty, who had charge of the people.

11Solomon brought Pharaoh's daughter up from the City of David to the house he had built for her, for he said, "No wife of mine shall live in the house of David king of Israel, for the places to which the ark of the LORD has come are holy."

The Service of the House

12Then Solomon offered burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar of the LORD that he had built before the porch,

13as the duty of each day required, offering according to the commandment of Moses on the sabbaths, the new moons and the appointed feasts three times a year: at the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the Festival of Weeks and the Festival of Booths.

14According to the rule of David his father, he appointed the divisions of the priests for their service, and the Levites for their duties, to praise and to minister before the priests as the duty of each day required, and the gatekeepers by their divisions at each gate, for so David the man of God had commanded.

15They did not turn aside from the king's command to the priests and the Levites in any matter, or concerning the treasuries.

16So all the work of Solomon was carried out, up to the day the foundation of the house of the LORD was laid, and until it was finished. The house of the LORD was complete.

Ships to Ophir

17Then Solomon went to Ezion-geber and to Eloth, on the shore of the sea in the land of Edom.

18Hiram sent him ships by his servants, and servants who knew the sea, and they went with Solomon's servants to Ophir. They took from there four hundred and fifty talents of gold and brought it to King Solomon.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "the cities that Hiram had given him" — Kings tells it the other way: King Solomon gave Hiram twenty cities in the land of Galilee, and Hiram did not like them (1 Kings 9:11–13). In Chronicles the cities come from Hiram to Solomon, who settles Israelites in them. The Greek agrees with the Hebrew of Chronicles. The text keeps the Hebrew of each.

  • v3 "Hamath-zobah" — Solomon's only campaign in either book. David had struck Hadadezer king of Zobah, toward Hamath (1 Chronicles 18:3).

  • vv7–9 the forced labor — as in 1 Kings 9:20–22. The peoples not destroyed in the conquest work for the king; Israelites serve as soldiers and officers. Kings also says that King Solomon raised forced labor from all Israel, thirty thousand men (1 Kings 5:13).

  • v10 "two hundred and fifty" — Kings has five hundred and fifty (1 Kings 9:23). The Greek of Chronicles also has two hundred and fifty.

  • v11 "the places to which the ark of the LORD has come are holy" — the only time Chronicles mentions Pharaoh's daughter, and the reason for moving her is its own: a foreign wife may not live where the ark has been. Kings says only that she went up to her house (1 Kings 9:24), and later, that King Solomon loved many foreign women, besides the daughter of Pharaoh (1 Kings 11:1).

  • v13 "three times a year: at the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the Festival of Weeks and the Festival of Booths" — the three feasts of Deuteronomy 16:16. Kings says three times a year and does not name them (1 Kings 9:25).

  • v14 "David the man of God" — the title of Moses (Deuteronomy 33:1; 1 Chronicles 23:14), given to David here and again only in Nehemiah 12:24 and 36, both times for the order of the singers.

  • v16 "up to the day the foundation… was laid, and until it was finished" — ad ha-yom musad beit YHWH ve-ad kelloto, until the day of the foundation… and until its finishing. The Greek has from the day it was founded until Solomon finished. The text keeps the Hebrew.

  • v18 "Hiram sent him ships… four hundred and fifty talents" — Kings has Solomon build the fleet and Hiram send seamen, and four hundred and twenty talents (1 Kings 9:26–28).

chapters.title: The Queen of Sheba and Solomon's Wealth
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 9

The Queen of Sheba

1When the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon, she came to Jerusalem to test Solomon with hard questions, with a very great retinue, with camels carrying spices and very much gold and precious stones. When she came to Solomon, she spoke with him of all that was on her heart.

2Solomon answered all her questions; there was nothing hidden from Solomon that he did not explain to her.

3When the queen of Sheba had seen the wisdom of Solomon, the house that he had built,

4the food of his table, the seating of his servants, the attendance of his ministers and their clothing, his cupbearers and their clothing, and the ascent by which he went up to the house of the LORD, there was no longer any spirit in her.

5She said to the king, "The report was true that I heard in my own land of your words and of your wisdom,

6but I did not believe their words until I came and my own eyes had seen it. Not even half the greatness of your wisdom was told me; you surpass the report that I heard.

7Happy are your men! Happy are these servants of yours, who stand continually before you and hear your wisdom!

8Blessed be the LORD your God, who has delighted in you and set you on His throne as king for the LORD your God! Because your God loved Israel, to establish them forever, He has made you king over them, to do justice and righteousness."

9Then she gave the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold, and a very great quantity of spices and precious stones. There were no spices like those the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.

10Moreover, the servants of Hiram and the servants of Solomon, who brought gold from Ophir, brought algum wood and precious stones.

11From the algum wood the king made steps for the house of the LORD and for the king's house, and lyres and harps for the singers. None like them had been seen before in the land of Judah.

12King Solomon gave to the queen of Sheba all that she desired, whatever she asked, besides what she had brought to the king. Then she turned and went back to her own land, she and her servants.

Solomon's Gold

13The weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred and sixty-six talents of gold,

14besides what the traders and merchants brought; and all the kings of Arabia and the governors of the land brought gold and silver to Solomon.

15King Solomon made two hundred large shields of beaten gold; six hundred shekels of beaten gold went into each shield.

16He made three hundred shields of beaten gold; three hundred shekels of gold went into each shield. The king put them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.

17The king also made a great throne of ivory and overlaid it with pure gold.

18The throne had six steps and a footstool of gold, which were fastened to the throne. On each side of the seat were armrests, and two lions standing beside the armrests.

19Twelve lions stood there on the six steps, one on each side. Nothing like it was made in any kingdom.

20All King Solomon's drinking vessels were of gold, and all the vessels of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were of pure gold. Silver was not considered as anything in the days of Solomon.

21For the king's ships went to Tarshish with the servants of Hiram. Once every three years the ships of Tarshish came, bringing gold, silver, ivory, apes and peacocks.

22So King Solomon exceeded all the kings of the earth in riches and in wisdom.

23All the kings of the earth sought the presence of Solomon to hear his wisdom, which God had put in his heart.

24Each of them brought his gift, articles of silver and articles of gold, garments, weapons, spices, horses and mules, so much year by year.

25Solomon had four thousand stalls for horses and chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen, whom he stationed in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.

26He ruled over all the kings from the River to the land of the Philistines and to the border of Egypt.

27The king made silver as common in Jerusalem as stones, and he made cedars as plentiful as the sycamore trees of the lowland.

28Horses were brought to Solomon from Egypt and from all the lands.

The Death of Solomon

29The rest of the acts of Solomon, from first to last, are they not written in the words of Nathan the prophet, in the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and in the visions of Iddo the seer concerning Jeroboam son of Nebat?

30Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel forty years.

31Solomon lay down with his fathers and was buried in the City of David his father, and Rehoboam his son reigned in his place.

Notes

  • vv1–28 and 1 Kings 10 — the same chapter; the English follows 1 Kings where the Hebrew is the same. Chronicles has the fame of Solomon without concerning the name of the LORD (1 Kings 10:1).

  • v4 "the ascent by which he went up to the house of the LORD" — va-aliyyato asher ya'aleh. Kings has ve-olato, his burnt offerings that he offered (1 Kings 10:5); the two words share their letters but one. The Greek of Chronicles has burnt offerings. The text keeps the Hebrew.

  • v8 "set you on His throne as king for the LORD your God" — Kings has the throne of Israel (1 Kings 10:9). In Chronicles the throne is the LORD's, as Solomon sat on the throne of the LORD as king (1 Chronicles 29:23).

  • vv10–11 "algum wood… steps" — algummim, which Kings spells almuggim (1 Kings 10:11); the tree is not known. Kings has supports, mis'ad; Chronicles has mesillot, raised ways or steps.

  • v18 "a footstool of gold" — kevesh, found only here. Kings has the top of the throne was rounded at the back (1 Kings 10:19).

  • v21 "the king's ships went to Tarshish" — Kings has a fleet of ships of Tarshish (1 Kings 10:22), the name of a kind of ship. Chronicles reads Tarshish as the place they sailed to.

  • v25 "four thousand stalls" — Kings has forty thousand stalls (1 Kings 4:26).

  • v26 "from the River to the land of the Philistines and to the border of Egypt" — as 1 Kings 4:21; the borders promised to Abram, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river Euphrates (Genesis 15:18).

  • vv29–31 "Nathan the prophet… Ahijah the Shilonite… Iddo the seer" — Kings cites the book of the acts of Solomon (1 Kings 11:41). Between Solomon's wealth and his death Kings tells of his foreign wives, his turning to other gods and the LORD's anger (1 Kings 11:1–40); Chronicles tells none of it. Iddo is written Ye'di and read Ye'do.

chapters.title: Israel Breaks Away
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 10

The Assembly at Shechem

1Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel had come to Shechem to make him king.

2And it came to pass, when Jeroboam son of Nebat heard of it — for he was in Egypt, where he had fled from King Solomon — that Jeroboam returned from Egypt.

3They sent and called him, and Jeroboam and all Israel came and spoke to Rehoboam, saying,

4"Your father made our yoke hard. Now lighten the hard service of your father and his heavy yoke that he put on us, and we will serve you."

5He said to them, "Come back to me in three days." So the people went away.

6King Rehoboam took counsel with the elders who had stood before Solomon his father while he was alive, saying, "How do you counsel me to answer this people?"

7They spoke to him, saying, "If you will be kind to this people and please them, and speak good words to them, they will be your servants for all time."

8But he abandoned the counsel that the elders gave him, and took counsel with the young men who had grown up with him and stood before him.

9He said to them, "What do you counsel that we answer this people who have said to me, 'Lighten the yoke that your father put on us'?"

10The young men who had grown up with him said to him, "Thus shall you say to the people who said to you, 'Your father made our yoke heavy, but you lighten it for us' — thus shall you say to them: 'My little finger is thicker than my father's loins.

11Now, whereas my father laid on you a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions.'"

12So Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, as the king had said, "Come back to me on the third day."

13The king answered them harshly. King Rehoboam abandoned the counsel of the elders,

14and spoke to them according to the counsel of the young men, saying, "I will make your yoke heavy, and I will add to it. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions."

15So the king did not listen to the people, for it was a turn of affairs from God, so that the LORD might establish His word that He spoke through Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat.

The Kingdom Divided

16When all Israel saw that the king did not listen to them, the people answered the king,
"What share do we have in David?
We have no inheritance in the son of Jesse.
Every man to your tents, Israel!
Now look to your own house, David."
So all Israel went to their tents.

17But as for the sons of Israel who lived in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam reigned over them.

18Then King Rehoboam sent Hadoram, who was over the forced labor, and the sons of Israel stoned him to death. King Rehoboam hurried to mount his chariot to flee to Jerusalem.

19So Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David to this day.

Notes

  • vv1–19 and 1 Kings 12:1–19 — the same chapter; the English follows 1 Kings where the Hebrew is the same. Chronicles does not go on to Jeroboam's crowning or his kingdom (1 Kings 12:20–33). From here it follows the kings of Judah alone, and Israel's kings appear only when they meet Judah's.

  • v2 "Jeroboam returned from Egypt" — va-yashov… mi-Mitsrayim. Kings has va-yeshev… be-Mitsrayim, stayed in Egypt (1 Kings 12:2); the two differ by one letter. Ahijah had told him he would rule ten tribes (1 Kings 11:29–39), and Chronicles names that word in v15.

  • v7 "If you will be kind to this people and please them" — im tihyeh le-tov la-am ha-zeh u-retsitam. Kings has If you will be a servant to this people today and serve them (1 Kings 12:7). Kings asks the king to serve; Chronicles asks him to be good to them.

  • v14 "I will make your yoke heavy" — akhbid, the king's own word. Kings has My father made your yoke heavy (1 Kings 12:14).

  • v15 "a turn of affairs from God" — nesibbah me-im ha-Elohim, a word found only here; Kings has sibbah me-im YHWH (1 Kings 12:15). The king's folly serves the word spoken through Ahijah.

  • v16 "What share do we have in David?… Every man to your tents, Israel!" — nearly the cry of Sheba's revolt against David, We have no share in David, no inheritance in the son of Jesse. Every man to his tents, Israel! (2 Samuel 20:1).

  • v18 "Hadoram, who was over the forced labor" — Kings has Adoram (1 Kings 12:18). The office is that of Adoniram under Solomon (1 Kings 4:6). The man sent to reason with the north is the man who ran the forced labor.

chapters.title: Rehoboam Strengthens Judah
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 11

Shemaiah's Word

1When Rehoboam came to Jerusalem, he assembled the house of Judah and Benjamin, a hundred and eighty thousand chosen warriors, to fight against Israel, to bring the kingdom back to Rehoboam.

2But the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah the man of God, saying,

3"Say to Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all Israel in Judah and Benjamin,

4'Thus says the LORD: You shall not go up or fight against your brothers. Return every man to his house, for this thing is from Me.'" So they listened to the words of the LORD and turned back from going against Jeroboam.

The Fortified Cities

5Rehoboam lived in Jerusalem, and he built cities for defense in Judah.

6He built Bethlehem, Etam, Tekoa,

7Beth-zur, Soco, Adullam,

8Gath, Mareshah, Ziph,

9Adoraim, Lachish, Azekah,

10Zorah, Aijalon and Hebron, fortified cities in Judah and in Benjamin.

11He strengthened the fortresses and put commanders in them, and stores of food, oil and wine.

12In every city he put shields and spears, and made them very strong. So Judah and Benjamin were his.

The Priests and Levites Come to Judah

13The priests and the Levites who were in all Israel took their stand with him from all their territory.

14For the Levites left their pasture lands and their holdings and came to Judah and Jerusalem, because Jeroboam and his sons had rejected them from serving as priests to the LORD,

15and he had appointed his own priests for the high places, for the goat-spirits and for the calves that he had made.

16After them, those from all the tribes of Israel who set their hearts to seek the LORD, the God of Israel, came to Jerusalem to sacrifice to the LORD, the God of their fathers.

17They strengthened the kingdom of Judah and made Rehoboam son of Solomon secure for three years, for they walked in the way of David and Solomon for three years.

Rehoboam's Family

18Rehoboam took as his wife Mahalath, the daughter of Jerimoth son of David, and Abihail the daughter of Eliab son of Jesse.

19She bore him sons: Jeush, Shemariah and Zaham.

20After her he took Maacah the daughter of Absalom, and she bore him Abijah, Attai, Ziza and Shelomith.

21Rehoboam loved Maacah the daughter of Absalom more than all his wives and secondary wives, for he took eighteen wives and sixty secondary wives, and fathered twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.

22Rehoboam appointed Abijah son of Maacah as chief, leader among his brothers, for he meant to make him king.

23He acted wisely and distributed some of all his sons through all the districts of Judah and Benjamin, in all the fortified cities. He gave them provisions in abundance, and sought many wives for them.

Notes

  • vv1–4 and 1 Kings 12:21–24 — the same account. Kings speaks to the house of Judah and Benjamin, and the rest of the people; Chronicles to all Israel in Judah and Benjamin (v3): the people loyal to David's house are Israel too.

  • vv5–12 the fortified cities — not in Kings. Fifteen towns, most of them south and west of Jerusalem. Five years later Shishak takes the fortified cities of Judah (12:4).

  • vv13–15 "Jeroboam… appointed his own priests for the high places, for the goat-spirits and for the calves" — Kings: he made priests from among all the people, who were not of the sons of Levi (1 Kings 12:31), and made two calves of gold (1 Kings 12:28). Se'irim, goat-spirits, is the word of the law that forbade them: They shall no longer offer their sacrifices to the goat-spirits (Leviticus 17:7).

  • v16 "who set their hearts to seek the LORD" — le-vaqqesh et YHWH. The faithful of the north come south, and the strength of Judah is counted in them.

  • v17 "for three years… for three years" — the Hebrew says it twice. The next chapter begins when the three years are over: he abandoned the instruction of the LORD (12:1).

  • v18 "Mahalath, the daughter of Jerimoth son of David" — written ben, son, read bat, daughter; the text follows the read form. Jerimoth is not among David's sons in 1 Chronicles 3. Abihail the daughter of Eliab may be a second wife or Mahalath's mother; the Hebrew does not say. Eliab is Jesse's firstborn (1 Chronicles 2:13).

  • v20 "Maacah the daughter of Absalom" — Kings: Maacah daughter of Abishalom (1 Kings 15:2). The next chapter of Chronicles names Abijah's mother Micaiah the daughter of Uriel of Gibeah (13:2).

Shemaiah's Word
When Rehoboam came to Jerusalem, he assembled the house of Judah and Benjamin, a hundred and eighty thousand chosen warriors, to fight against Israel, to bring the kingdom back to Rehoboam.
But the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah the man of God, saying,
"Say to Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all Israel in Judah and Benjamin,

'Thus says the LORD: You shall not go up or fight against your brothers. Return every man to his house, for this thing is from Me.'" So they listened to the words of the LORD and turned back from going against Jeroboam.
The Fortified Cities
Rehoboam lived in Jerusalem, and he built cities for defense in Judah.
He built Bethlehem, Etam, Tekoa,
Beth-zur, Soco, Adullam,
Gath, Mareshah, Ziph,
Adoraim, Lachish, Azekah,
Zorah, Aijalon and Hebron, fortified cities in Judah and in Benjamin.
He strengthened the fortresses and put commanders in them, and stores of food, oil and wine.
In every city he put shields and spears, and made them very strong. So Judah and Benjamin were his.
The Priests and Levites Come to Judah
The priests and the Levites who were in all Israel took their stand with him from all their territory.
For the Levites left their pasture lands and their holdings and came to Judah and Jerusalem, because Jeroboam and his sons had rejected them from serving as priests to the LORD,
and he had appointed his own priests for the high places, for the goat-spirits and for the calves that he had made.
After them, those from all the tribes of Israel who set their hearts to seek the LORD, the God of Israel, came to Jerusalem to sacrifice to the LORD, the God of their fathers.

She bore him sons: Jeush, Shemariah and Zaham.
After her he took Maacah the daughter of Absalom, and she bore him Abijah, Attai, Ziza and Shelomith.
Rehoboam loved Maacah the daughter of Absalom more than all his wives and secondary wives, for he took eighteen wives and sixty secondary wives, and fathered twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.

He acted wisely and distributed some of all his sons through all the districts of Judah and Benjamin, in all the fortified cities. He gave them provisions in abundance, and sought many wives for them.

chapters.title: Shishak Comes Up Against Jerusalem
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 12

Shishak's Invasion

1And it came to pass, when the kingdom of Rehoboam was established and he was strong, that he forsook the instruction of the LORD, and all Israel with him.

2And it came to pass in the fifth year of King Rehoboam that Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, because they had broken faith with the LORD,

3with twelve hundred chariots and sixty thousand horsemen. The people who came with him from Egypt were without number: Libyans, Sukkiim and Cushites.

4He took the fortified cities of Judah and came as far as Jerusalem.

5Then Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam and to the officials of Judah, who had gathered at Jerusalem because of Shishak, and said to them, "Thus says the LORD: You have forsaken Me, so I have forsaken you into the hand of Shishak."

6The officials of Israel and the king humbled themselves and said, "The LORD is righteous."

7When the LORD saw that they had humbled themselves, the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah, saying, "They have humbled themselves. I will not destroy them, but I will grant them some deliverance, and My wrath shall not be poured out on Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak.

8But they shall be his servants, so that they may know My service and the service of the kingdoms of the lands."

9So Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem. He took away the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the king's house; he took away everything. He also took away the shields of gold that Solomon had made.

10King Rehoboam made shields of bronze in their place, and committed them to the hands of the officers of the guard, who kept the door of the king's house.

11As often as the king went into the house of the LORD, the guard came and carried them, and brought them back to the guardroom.

12When he humbled himself, the anger of the LORD turned away from him, so as not to destroy him completely. In Judah, too, there were good things.

The End of Rehoboam's Reign

13So King Rehoboam strengthened himself in Jerusalem and reigned. Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city that the LORD had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel to put His name there. His mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite.

14He did evil, for he did not set his heart to seek the LORD.

15The acts of Rehoboam, from first to last, are they not written in the words of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer, by genealogy? There were wars between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continually.

16Rehoboam lay down with his fathers and was buried in the City of David, and Abijah his son reigned in his place.

Notes

  • v1 "when the kingdom of Rehoboam was established and he was strong, that he forsook the instruction of the LORD" — the three years of 11:17 are over. Strength comes first and forsaking after, the order Moses warned of: when you have eaten and are satisfied… your heart is not lifted up and you forget the LORD your God (Deuteronomy 8:12–14).

  • v2 "because they had broken faith with the LORD" — ki ma'alu ba-YHWH, the charge on which Saul died (1 Chronicles 10:13). Kings gives the year and the plunder (1 Kings 14:25–28); Chronicles gives the reason.

  • v5 "You have forsaken Me, so I have forsaken you" — azavtem oti ve-af ani azavti etkhem, the same verb both ways, as David warned Solomon: if you forsake Him, He will reject you forever (1 Chronicles 28:9).

  • vv6–7, 12 "humbled themselves" — va-yikkane'u, the first time the word of 7:14 is kept: if My people… humble themselves… I will hear. The LORD answers with a measure, some deliverance, ki-me'at li-fleitah.

  • v8 "so that they may know My service and the service of the kingdoms of the lands" — avodati ve-avodat mamlekhot ha-arets, one word for both: Judah will learn by serving Egypt what serving the LORD was.

  • v9 "the shields of gold that Solomon had made" — the two hundred large shields and three hundred shields of 9:15–16.

  • v12 "In Judah, too, there were good things" — ve-gam bi-Yhudah hayah devarim tovim, set beside so as not to destroy him completely.

  • v15 "by genealogy" — le-hityachesh, the word for enrolling by descent (1 Chronicles 5:17; 9:1). Why it stands here after the names of two prophets is not clear.

chapters.title: Abijah's War with Jeroboam
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 13

Abijah King of Judah

1In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam, Abijah began to reign over Judah.

2He reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Micaiah the daughter of Uriel of Gibeah. There was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.

3Abijah went out to battle with an army of mighty men of war, four hundred thousand chosen men, and Jeroboam drew up his battle line against him with eight hundred thousand chosen men, mighty men of valor.

Abijah's Speech on Mount Zemaraim

4Abijah stood up on Mount Zemaraim, which is in the hill country of Ephraim, and said, "Hear me, Jeroboam and all Israel!

5Ought you not to know that the LORD, the God of Israel, gave the kingship over Israel to David forever, to him and to his sons, by a covenant of salt?

6Yet Jeroboam son of Nebat, a servant of Solomon son of David, rose up and rebelled against his lord.

7Worthless men gathered around him, scoundrels, and they proved too strong for Rehoboam son of Solomon, when Rehoboam was young and tender of heart and could not hold his own against them.

8And now you think you can hold your own against the kingdom of the LORD in the hand of the sons of David, because you are a great multitude and have with you the golden calves that Jeroboam made you for gods.

9Have you not driven out the priests of the LORD, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and made priests for yourselves like the peoples of other lands? Whoever comes to consecrate himself with a young bull and seven rams becomes a priest of what are no gods.

10But as for us, the LORD is our God, and we have not forsaken Him. We have priests ministering to the LORD who are sons of Aaron, and Levites at their work.

11They burn burnt offerings to the LORD every morning and every evening, and fragrant incense, and set out the bread on the pure table, and the golden lampstand with its lamps to burn every evening. For we keep the charge of the LORD our God, but you have forsaken Him.

12God is with us at our head, and His priests with the battle trumpets to sound the alarm against you. Sons of Israel, do not fight against the LORD, the God of your fathers, for you will not succeed."

The Battle

13But Jeroboam had sent an ambush around to come at them from behind, so that his army was in front of Judah and the ambush behind them.

14When Judah turned, the battle was before them and behind. They cried out to the LORD, and the priests blew the trumpets.

15Then the men of Judah raised the battle shout. And it came to pass, as the men of Judah shouted, that God struck down Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah.

16The sons of Israel fled before Judah, and God gave them into their hand.

17Abijah and his people struck them with a great slaughter, and five hundred thousand chosen men of Israel fell slain.

18So the sons of Israel were humbled at that time, and the sons of Judah prevailed, because they relied on the LORD, the God of their fathers.

19Abijah pursued Jeroboam and took cities from him: Bethel and its villages, Jeshanah and its villages, and Ephrain and its villages.

20Jeroboam did not recover his strength again in the days of Abijah. The LORD struck him, and he died.

21But Abijah grew strong. He took fourteen wives and fathered twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.

22The rest of the acts of Abijah, his ways and his sayings, are written in the account of the prophet Iddo.

Notes

  • vv1–2 and 1 Kings 15:1–8 — Kings calls him Abijam and judges him in one line: He walked in all the sins that his father had done before him (1 Kings 15:3). Chronicles gives no verdict and tells instead of his speech and his victory. His mother is Micaiah the daughter of Uriel of Gibeah; 11:20 and Kings name her Maacah.

  • v5 "by a covenant of salt" — berit melach, the phrase of the priests' portion: It is a covenant of salt forever before the LORD (Numbers 18:19). Salt does not spoil; the covenant with David's house is meant to last the same way.

  • v7 "young and tender of heart" — na'ar ve-rakh levav, the words David used of Solomon, young and tender (1 Chronicles 22:5). Rehoboam was forty-one when he began to reign (12:13); the word is about his nerve, not his age.

  • v8 "the kingdom of the LORD in the hand of the sons of David" — the kingdom is the LORD's, as in the promise, over My house and over My kingdom (1 Chronicles 17:14).

  • v9 "to consecrate himself… a priest of what are no gods" — le-mallot yado, to fill his hand, the words for ordaining a priest (1 Chronicles 29:5). Lo elohim, no gods: the Greek has a priest to what is not God.

  • v12 "His priests with the battle trumpets to sound the alarm" — the law of the trumpets: When you go to war… you shall sound a blast on the trumpets, and you will be remembered before the LORD your God (Numbers 10:9). The trumpets sound in v14, and God strikes in v15.

  • v18 "because they relied on the LORD" — ki nish'anu, the word on which Asa's reign will turn: we rely on You (14:11), and then because you relied on the king of Aram and did not rely on the LORD (16:7).

  • v20 "The LORD struck him, and he died" — Kings says only that Jeroboam lay down with his fathers (1 Kings 14:20).

  • v22 "the account of the prophet Iddo" — midrash, from darash, to seek, to inquire, the word Chronicles uses for seeking the LORD. Midrash is found only here and in 24:27.

chapters.title: Asa and Zerah the Cushite
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 14

Asa Seeks the LORD

1Abijah lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in the City of David, and Asa his son reigned in his place. In his days the land had rest for ten years.

2Asa did what was good and right in the eyes of the LORD his God.

3He removed the foreign altars and the high places, broke down the pillars and cut down the Asherim.

4He told Judah to seek the LORD, the God of their fathers, and to do the instruction and the commandment.

5He removed the high places and the incense altars from all the cities of Judah, and the kingdom had rest under him.

6He built fortified cities in Judah, for the land had rest. There was no war against him in those years, for the LORD had given him rest.

7He said to Judah, "Let us build these cities and surround them with walls and towers, gates and bars. The land is still ours, because we have sought the LORD our God. We have sought Him, and He has given us rest on every side." So they built and prospered.

8Asa had an army that carried shield and spear: from Judah three hundred thousand, and from Benjamin two hundred and eighty thousand who carried shields and drew the bow. All these were mighty men of valor.

The Battle at Mareshah

9Zerah the Cushite came out against them with an army of a million men and three hundred chariots, and came as far as Mareshah.

10Asa went out to meet him, and they drew up for battle in the Valley of Zephathah at Mareshah.

11Asa called to the LORD his God and said, "O LORD, there is none besides You to help, between the mighty and those who have no strength. Help us, O LORD our God, for we rely on You, and in Your name we have come against this multitude. O LORD, You are our God; do not let man prevail against You."

12So the LORD struck down the Cushites before Asa and before Judah, and the Cushites fled.

13Asa and the people with him pursued them as far as Gerar. So many Cushites fell that none of them was left alive, for they were shattered before the LORD and before His army. Judah carried away a very great amount of spoil.

14They struck all the cities around Gerar, for the fear of the LORD was on them. They plundered all the cities, for there was much plunder in them.

15They also struck the tents of the herdsmen, and carried off sheep in abundance and camels, and returned to Jerusalem.

Notes

  • v1 the numbering — in the Hebrew this verse is 13:23, and vv2–15 are 14:1–14. The text follows the English numbering.

  • v1 "the land had rest for ten years" — shaqtah ha-arets, the refrain of Judges, The land had rest forty years (Judges 3:11). It is said again in v6. Kings has no such words for Asa (1 Kings 15:9–15).

  • vv3–5 "the foreign altars and the high places… the incense altars" — chammanim, the word of the curse, I will destroy your high places and cut down your incense altars (Leviticus 26:30). Kings says the opposite of v5: the high places were not taken away (1 Kings 15:14), and Chronicles itself says in 15:17 that they were not removed from Israel.

  • v7 "because we have sought the LORD… He has given us rest on every side" — darashnu… va-yanach lanu. The rest promised for Solomon's days, I will give him rest from all his enemies around him (1 Chronicles 22:9), comes to the king who seeks.

  • v9 "Zerah the Cushite… a million men" — not in Kings. Cush is the land south of Egypt; Shishak's army had Cushites in it too (12:3).

  • v11 "between the mighty and those who have no strength… we rely on You" — bein rav le-ein koach: for the LORD, the size of the army makes no difference. Nish'annu, we rely, the word of Abijah's victory (13:18), and the word on which Asa will fail (16:7).

  • v11 "do not let man prevail against You" — enosh, mortal man. The battle is set as one between the LORD and a man, not between two armies.

  • v14 "the fear of the LORD was on them" — pachad YHWH. It falls on the cities of Gerar here, on the kingdoms around Judah in Jehoshaphat's day (17:10), and Jehoshaphat asks it of his judges (19:7).

chapters.title: Asa's Covenant
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 15

Azariah's Word

1The Spirit of God came on Azariah son of Oded,

2and he went out to meet Asa and said to him, "Hear me, Asa, and all Judah and Benjamin. The LORD is with you while you are with Him. If you seek Him, He will be found by you, but if you forsake Him, He will forsake you.

3For many days Israel was without the true God, without a priest to teach and without instruction.

4But when in their distress they turned to the LORD, the God of Israel, and sought Him, He was found by them.

5In those times there was no peace for anyone who went out or came in, for great turmoil was on all the inhabitants of the lands.

6They were crushed, nation by nation and city by city, for God troubled them with every kind of distress.

7But you, be strong, and do not let your hands go slack, for there is a reward for your work."

The Reform and the Oath

8When Asa heard these words and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he took courage and put away the loathsome things from all the land of Judah and Benjamin and from the cities he had taken in the hill country of Ephraim. He restored the altar of the LORD that was in front of the porch of the LORD.

9He gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and those from Ephraim, Manasseh and Simeon who lived as guests among them, for many had deserted to him from Israel when they saw that the LORD his God was with him.

10They gathered at Jerusalem in the third month of the fifteenth year of Asa's reign.

11On that day they sacrificed to the LORD, from the spoil they had brought, seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep.

12They entered into a covenant to seek the LORD, the God of their fathers, with all their heart and with all their soul,

13and that whoever would not seek the LORD, the God of Israel, should be put to death, whether small or great, whether man or woman.

14They swore an oath to the LORD with a loud voice, with shouting, with trumpets and with rams' horns.

15All Judah rejoiced over the oath, for they had sworn with all their heart and had sought Him with all their desire, and He was found by them. The LORD gave them rest on every side.

Maacah Removed

16King Asa also removed Maacah his mother from being queen mother, because she had made a horrid image for Asherah. Asa cut down her horrid image, crushed it and burned it at the Kidron Valley.

17But the high places were not removed from Israel. Nevertheless, the heart of Asa was whole all his days.

18He brought into the house of God the things his father had dedicated and the things he himself had dedicated, silver and gold and vessels.

19There was no more war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa's reign.

Notes

  • v2 "If you seek Him, He will be found by you, but if you forsake Him, He will forsake you" — the words of David to Solomon, If you seek Him, He will be found by you; but if you forsake Him, He will reject you forever (1 Chronicles 28:9), now said to the whole people. Vv4 and 15 show it kept: He was found by them.

  • v3 "For many days Israel was without the true God, without a priest to teach and without instruction" — three withouts, le-lo. The same shape stands in Hosea 3:4, For many days the sons of Israel shall live without king and without prince, without sacrifice and without pillar. Whether Azariah speaks of the days of the judges or of a time to come, the Hebrew does not say; the verbs have no tense of their own.

  • v5 "no peace for anyone who went out or came in" — ein shalom la-yotse ve-la-ba, the words of Zechariah 8:10 for the days before the house was rebuilt.

  • v8 "the prophecy of Oded the prophet" — v1 gives the words to Azariah son of Oded; here the Hebrew has Oded, and the Greek Adad. The text keeps the Hebrew. Ha-shiqqutsim, the loathsome things.

  • v10 "in the third month" — the month Israel came to Sinai, In the third month after the sons of Israel went out of the land of Egypt (Exodus 19:1), where the first covenant was made.

  • v13 "whoever would not seek the LORD… should be put to death, whether small or great, whether man or woman" — the law against serving other gods, a man or a woman who does what is evil in the eyes of the LORD your God, transgressing His covenant… you shall stone them (Deuteronomy 17:2–5). Not seeking the LORD is counted as turning to another.

  • vv16–18 and 1 Kings 15:13–15 — the same account. Gevirah, queen mother: the king's mother held a rank of her own, and Asa took it from her.

  • v17 "But the high places were not removed from Israel" — as 1 Kings 15:14. In 14:5 Asa removed the high places… from all the cities of Judah; here they remain in Israel. The text keeps both.

  • v19 "no more war until the thirty-fifth year" — Kings says There was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days (1 Kings 15:16).

For many days Israel was without the true God, without a priest to teach and without instruction.
But when in their distress they turned to the LORD, the God of Israel, and sought Him, He was found by them.
In those times there was no peace for anyone who went out or came in, for great turmoil was on all the inhabitants of the lands.
They were crushed, nation by nation and city by city, for God troubled them with every kind of distress.
But you, be strong, and do not let your hands go slack, for there is a reward for your work."

When Asa heard these words and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he took courage and put away the loathsome things from all the land of Judah and Benjamin and from the cities he had taken in the hill country of Ephraim. He restored the altar of the LORD that was in front of the porch of the LORD.

He gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and those from Ephraim, Manasseh and Simeon who lived as guests among them, for many had deserted to him from Israel when they saw that the LORD his God was with him.
They gathered at Jerusalem in the third month of the fifteenth year of Asa's reign.
On that day they sacrificed to the LORD, from the spoil they had brought, seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep.
They entered into a covenant to seek the LORD, the God of their fathers, with all their heart and with all their soul,
and that whoever would not seek the LORD, the God of Israel, should be put to death, whether small or great, whether man or woman.
They swore an oath to the LORD with a loud voice, with shouting, with trumpets and with rams' horns.
All Judah rejoiced over the oath, for they had sworn with all their heart and had sought Him with all their desire, and He was found by them. The LORD gave them rest on every side.
