King Asa also removed Maacah his mother from being queen mother, because she had made a horrid image for Asherah. Asa cut down her horrid image, crushed it and burned it at the Kidron Valley.
But the high places were not removed from Israel. Nevertheless, the heart of Asa was whole all his days.
He brought into the house of God the things his father had dedicated and the things he himself had dedicated, silver and gold and vessels.
There was no more war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa's reign.

chapters.title: Asa Relies on Aram
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 16

The Treaty with Ben-hadad

1In the thirty-sixth year of Asa's reign, Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah and built Ramah, to prevent anyone from going out or coming in to Asa king of Judah.

2Then Asa brought out silver and gold from the treasuries of the house of the LORD and of the king's house, and sent them to Ben-hadad king of Aram, who lived in Damascus, saying,

3"Let there be a covenant between me and you, as there was between my father and your father. I am sending you silver and gold. Go, break your covenant with Baasha king of Israel, so that he will withdraw from me."

4Ben-hadad listened to King Asa and sent the commanders of his armies against the cities of Israel, and they struck Ijon, Dan, Abel-maim and all the store cities of Naphtali.

5And it came to pass, when Baasha heard of it, that he stopped building Ramah and let his work cease.

6Then King Asa took all Judah, and they carried away the stones of Ramah and its timber, with which Baasha had been building, and with them he built Geba and Mizpah.

Hanani the Seer

7At that time Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Judah and said to him, "Because you relied on the king of Aram and did not rely on the LORD your God, the army of the king of Aram has escaped from your hand.

8Were not the Cushites and the Libyans a huge army, with chariots and horsemen in great number? Yet because you relied on the LORD, He gave them into your hand.

9For the eyes of the LORD run to and fro through the whole earth, to show Himself strong for those whose heart is whole toward Him. You have acted foolishly in this, for from now on you will have wars."

10Asa was angry with the seer and put him in the stocks, for he was in a rage with him over this. At that time Asa also crushed some of the people.

The Death of Asa

11The acts of Asa, from first to last, are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.

12In the thirty-ninth year of his reign Asa was diseased in his feet, and his disease became severe. Yet even in his disease he did not seek the LORD, but the healers.

13Asa lay down with his fathers, dying in the forty-first year of his reign.

14They buried him in his own tomb, which he had cut for himself in the City of David. They laid him on a bier filled with spices and various kinds of ointment prepared by the perfumer's art, and they made a very great fire in his honor.

Notes

  • vv1–6 and 1 Kings 15:17–22 — the same account. Chronicles dates it to the thirty-sixth year of Asa; Kings has Baasha's son Elah reigning already in the twenty-sixth year of Asa (1 Kings 16:8). The text keeps the Hebrew of each.

  • v7 "Because you relied on the king of Aram and did not rely on the LORD" — be-hisha'enkha… ve-lo nish'anta, the word of Asa's own prayer at Mareshah, we rely on You (14:11). Not in Kings, which tells the treaty without a word of judgment.

  • v8 "the Cushites and the Libyans" — Zerah's army of 14:9–15. Because you relied on the LORD, He gave them into your hand: the seer holds up Asa's own victory against him.

  • v9 "the eyes of the LORD run to and fro through the whole earth" — einei YHWH meshotetot be-khol ha-arets, the words of Zechariah 4:10, the eyes of the LORD, which run to and fro through the whole earth. Whole toward Him, shalem, the word said of Asa's heart in 15:17.

  • v9 "You have acted foolishly" — niskalta, Samuel's word to Saul, You have acted foolishly. You have not kept the command of the LORD your God (1 Samuel 13:13).

  • v10 "put him in the stocks" — beit ha-mahpekhet, the word of Jeremiah 20:2, where Pashhur put him in the stocks that were in the upper Benjamin Gate. A king of David's line does to a seer what a priest later does to a prophet.

  • v12 "he did not seek the LORD, but the healers" — lo darash et YHWH ki ba-rof'im. The king whose reign was built on seeking the LORD (14:4, 7; 15:2, 12) ends by seeking elsewhere, though the LORD named Himself your healer, rof'ekha (Exodus 15:26).

  • v14 "a very great fire in his honor" — serefah, a burning made for a king at his burial, as Jeremiah promises Zedekiah, as they burned for your fathers, the former kings… so they will burn for you (Jeremiah 34:5). Jehoram is denied it: his people made no fire for him like the fire for his fathers (21:19).

chapters.title: Jehoshaphat Teaches Judah
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 17

Jehoshaphat Strengthened

1Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his place and strengthened himself against Israel.

2He placed troops in all the fortified cities of Judah, and set garrisons in the land of Judah and in the cities of Ephraim that Asa his father had taken.

3The LORD was with Jehoshaphat, because he walked in the earlier ways of David his father and did not seek the Baals,

4but sought the God of his father and walked in His commandments, and not as Israel did.

5So the LORD established the kingdom in his hand. All Judah brought tribute to Jehoshaphat, and he had riches and honor in abundance.

6His heart was lifted up in the ways of the LORD, and he again removed the high places and the Asherim from Judah.

Teachers in the Cities

7In the third year of his reign he sent his officials, Ben-hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel and Micaiah, to teach in the cities of Judah.

8With them were the Levites Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah and Tob-adonijah, the Levites, and with them the priests Elishama and Jehoram.

9They taught in Judah, having the book of the instruction of the LORD with them. They went around through all the cities of Judah and taught among the people.

Tribute and Troops

10The fear of the LORD fell on all the kingdoms of the lands around Judah, and they did not make war against Jehoshaphat.

11Some of the Philistines brought Jehoshaphat gifts and silver as tribute, and the Arabians also brought him flocks: seven thousand seven hundred rams and seven thousand seven hundred goats.

12Jehoshaphat grew steadily greater. He built fortresses and store cities in Judah,

13and he had much work in the cities of Judah, and soldiers, mighty men of valor, in Jerusalem.

14This was their muster by their fathers' houses. Of Judah, the commanders of thousands: Adnah the commander, and with him three hundred thousand mighty men of valor;

15next to him Jehohanan the commander, and with him two hundred and eighty thousand;

16and next to him Amasiah son of Zichri, who offered himself willingly to the LORD, and with him two hundred thousand mighty men of valor.

17Of Benjamin: Eliada, a mighty man of valor, and with him two hundred thousand armed with bow and shield;

18and next to him Jehozabad, and with him a hundred and eighty thousand equipped for war.

19These were the men who served the king, besides those the king had placed in the fortified cities throughout all Judah.

Notes

  • vv1–19 — not in Kings, which gives Jehoshaphat's reign a summary of ten verses (1 Kings 22:41–50) and tells him mostly beside Ahab.

  • v3 "the earlier ways of David his father" — darkhei David aviv ha-rishonim. The Greek has the ways of his father, the earlier ones, without David, and then the father is Asa, whose earlier years were faithful and his last were not (16:7–12). The text keeps the Hebrew.

  • v6 "His heart was lifted up in the ways of the LORD" — va-yigbah libbo. Everywhere else in the book the phrase is pride: Uzziah's heart was lifted up, to his destruction (26:16), and Hezekiah's (32:25). Here alone it is good: his heart was raised high in the LORD's ways.

  • v6 "he again removed the high places" — 20:33 says the high places were not removed, as Kings does (1 Kings 22:43). The text keeps both.

  • vv7–9 "having the book of the instruction of the LORD with them" — sefer torat YHWH, carried from town to town by officials, Levites and priests together. The blessing of Levi: They teach Your rules to Jacob (Deuteronomy 33:10). The same phrase names the book found in Josiah's day (34:14).

  • v10 "The fear of the LORD fell on all the kingdoms" — pachad YHWH, as on the cities around Gerar in Asa's war (14:14). Here it comes without a battle.

  • v16 "who offered himself willingly to the LORD" — ha-mitnaddev, the word of Deborah's song, when the people offer themselves willingly (Judges 5:2, 9), and of the gifts for the house (1 Chronicles 29:5–9).

chapters.title: Micaiah and the Death of Ahab
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 18

The Alliance with Ahab

1Jehoshaphat had riches and honor in abundance, and he made a marriage alliance with Ahab.

2After some years he went down to Ahab in Samaria. Ahab slaughtered sheep and oxen in abundance for him and for the people who were with him, and he enticed him to go up against Ramoth-gilead.

3Ahab king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, "Will you go with me to Ramoth-gilead?" He said to him, "I am as you are, and my people as your people; we will be with you in the battle."

4But Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "Inquire first for the word of the LORD."

5Then the king of Israel gathered the prophets, four hundred men, and said to them, "Shall we go to battle against Ramoth-gilead, or shall I refrain?" They said, "Go up, for God will give it into the hand of the king."

Micaiah Son of Imlah

6But Jehoshaphat said, "Is there not here another prophet of the LORD, of whom we may inquire?"

7The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "There is yet one man by whom we may inquire of the LORD, but I hate him, for he never prophesies good concerning me, but always evil. He is Micaiah son of Imla." Jehoshaphat said, "Let not the king say so."

8Then the king of Israel called an officer and said, "Bring Micaiah son of Imla quickly."

9The king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting each on his throne, dressed in their robes; they were sitting at the threshing floor at the entrance of the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets were prophesying before them.

10Zedekiah son of Chenaanah made for himself horns of iron and said, "Thus says the LORD: 'With these you shall gore the Arameans until they are destroyed.'"

11All the prophets prophesied so, saying, "Go up to Ramoth-gilead and prosper; the LORD will give it into the hand of the king."

12The messenger who went to call Micaiah said to him, "The words of the prophets with one mouth are good for the king. Let your word be like one of theirs, and speak good."

13But Micaiah said, "As the LORD lives, what my God says, that I will speak."

14When he came to the king, the king said to him, "Micah, shall we go to battle against Ramoth-gilead, or shall I refrain?" He said, "Go up and prosper; they will be given into your hand."

15But the king said to him, "How many times shall I make you swear that you speak to me nothing but the truth in the name of the LORD?"

16So he said, "I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains, like sheep that have no shepherd. Then the LORD said, 'These have no master; let each return to his home in peace.'"

17The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Did I not tell you that he would not prophesy good concerning me, but evil?"

18Micaiah said, "Therefore hear the word of the LORD: I saw the LORD sitting on His throne, and all the host of heaven standing on His right hand and on His left.

19The LORD said, 'Who will entice Ahab king of Israel, so that he may go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead?' One said one thing, and another said another.

20Then a spirit came forward and stood before the LORD and said, 'I will entice him.' The LORD said to him, 'By what means?'

21He said, 'I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.' He said, 'You shall entice him, and you shall succeed. Go out and do so.'

22So now the LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouth of these your prophets, and the LORD has spoken evil concerning you."

23Then Zedekiah son of Chenaanah came near and struck Micaiah on the cheek and said, "Which way did the Spirit of the LORD pass from me to speak to you?"

24Micaiah said, "You shall see on that day, when you go into an inner room to hide yourself."

25The king of Israel said, "Take Micaiah and bring him back to Amon the governor of the city and to Joash the king's son,

26and say, 'Thus says the king: Put this man in prison, and feed him with a scant ration of bread and water until I return in peace.'"

27Micaiah said, "If you return in peace at all, the LORD has not spoken by me." Then he said, "Hear, all you peoples!"

The Battle at Ramoth-gilead

28So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up to Ramoth-gilead.

29The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "I will disguise myself and go into battle, but you wear your robes." So the king of Israel disguised himself, and they went into battle.

30Now the king of Aram had commanded the captains of his chariots, "Fight with neither small nor great, but only with the king of Israel."

31And it came to pass, when the captains of the chariots saw Jehoshaphat, that they said, "It is the king of Israel." So they turned to fight against him, and Jehoshaphat cried out. The LORD helped him, and God drew them away from him.

32And it came to pass, when the captains of the chariots saw that it was not the king of Israel, that they turned back from pursuing him.

33But a certain man drew his bow at random and struck the king of Israel between the joints of his armor. So he said to the driver of his chariot, "Turn your hand and carry me out of the battle, for I am wounded."

34The battle grew hot that day, and the king of Israel propped himself up in his chariot facing the Arameans until evening. He died as the sun went down.

Notes

  • vv1–34 and 1 Kings 22:1–35 — the same account; the English follows 1 Kings where the Hebrew is the same. Chronicles tells it as part of Jehoshaphat's story and ends with Ahab's death, without the dogs and his burial (1 Kings 22:36–40).

  • vv1–2 "he made a marriage alliance with Ahab… and he enticed him" — va-yitchatten, the marriage of Jehoshaphat's son Jehoram to Ahab's daughter (21:6). Va-yesitehu, enticed him, is the verb of 1 Chronicles 21:1, where Satan incited David. The feast at Samaria is how Jehoshaphat is drawn in. Not in Kings.

  • v10 "horns of iron… With these you shall gore the Arameans" — the picture of Moses' blessing on Joseph, With them he gores the peoples (Deuteronomy 33:17), acted out.

  • v16 "like sheep that have no shepherd" — Moses' words when he asked for a leader (Numbers 27:17). The king dies at sunset (v34).

  • vv18–22 "a spirit came forward… a lying spirit" — ha-ruach, the spirit, one of the host of v18, not the Spirit of the LORD; lowercase, as in 1 Kings 22:21. Zedekiah answers with the Spirit of the LORD (v23).

  • v27 "Hear, all you peoples!" — shim'u ammim kullam, the first words of the book of Micah (Micah 1:2), whose name is a short form of Micaiah. The king calls him Micah in v14.

  • v31 "The LORD helped him, and God drew them away from him" — not in Kings, where Jehoshaphat cried out and the captains simply see their mistake (1 Kings 22:32–33). Va-yesitem, drew them away, is the verb of v2: Ahab enticed Jehoshaphat into the battle, and God enticed the enemy away from him.

  • v34 "propped himself up… until evening. He died as the sun went down" — Kings has the blood of the wound ran into the bottom of the chariot (1 Kings 22:35); Chronicles leaves it out.

chapters.title: Jehoshaphat Appoints Judges
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 19

Jehu Son of Hanani

1Jehoshaphat king of Judah returned in peace to his house in Jerusalem.

2Jehu son of Hanani the seer went out to meet him and said to King Jehoshaphat, "Should you help the wicked and love those who hate the LORD? Because of this, wrath has gone out against you from the LORD.

3Yet good things are found in you, for you have removed the Asherahs from the land and have set your heart to seek God."

Judges in the Land

4Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem. He went out again among the people, from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim, and brought them back to the LORD, the God of their fathers.

5He appointed judges in the land, in all the fortified cities of Judah, city by city.

6He said to the judges, "Consider what you are doing, for you do not judge for man but for the LORD, and He is with you when you give judgment.

7Now let the fear of the LORD be on you. Take care what you do, for with the LORD our God there is no injustice, no partiality and no taking of bribes."

The Court in Jerusalem

8In Jerusalem also Jehoshaphat appointed some of the Levites and the priests and the heads of the fathers' houses of Israel, to give judgment for the LORD and to decide disputes. They lived in Jerusalem.

9He charged them, saying, "This is how you shall act: in the fear of the LORD, faithfully and with a whole heart.

10Whenever a case comes to you from your brothers who live in their cities, between blood and blood, between instruction and commandment, statutes and rules, you shall warn them, so that they do not incur guilt before the LORD and wrath come on you and your brothers. Do this, and you will not incur guilt.

11Amariah the chief priest is over you in every matter of the LORD, and Zebadiah son of Ishmael, the leader of the house of Judah, in every matter of the king. The Levites will serve you as officials. Be strong and act, and may the LORD be with the good."

Notes

  • vv1–11 — not in Kings. The king's name, Yehoshafat, is the LORD judges, from shafat, the verb of this chapter: judges, shoftim (v5), you do not judge (v6).

  • v2 "Jehu son of Hanani the seer" — the son of the seer Asa put in the stocks for rebuking him (16:7–10). Should you help the wicked and love those who hate the LORD?: the alliance with Ahab of chapter 18.

  • v3 "good things are found in you" — devarim tovim, the words said of Judah under Rehoboam (12:12). The wrath of v2 is not withdrawn; it is set beside them.

  • v4 "from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim" — the old saying for the whole land is from Dan to Beersheba; the kingdom of Judah now reaches only to Ephraim.

  • vv5–7 "judges… in all the fortified cities… no injustice, no partiality and no taking of bribes" — the law of Deuteronomy: Judges and officials you shall appoint for yourself in all your towns (Deuteronomy 16:18); the judgment is God's (1:17); the LORD shows no partiality and takes no bribe (10:17).

  • vv8–10 "between blood and blood" — bein dam le-dam, the words of the law of the central court: If a case is too hard for you in judgment — between blood and blood, between claim and claim… then you shall… go up to the place that the LORD your God will choose (Deuteronomy 17:8).   • v11 "in every matter of the LORD… in every matter of the king" — the division David made beyond the Jordan, for every matter of God and every matter of the king (1 Chronicles 26:32): a priest over the one, a leader of Judah over the other.

chapters.title: The Battle Is God's
chapters.html:
2 Chronicles 20

The Army from Beyond the Sea

1And it came to pass after this that the sons of Moab and the sons of Ammon, and with them some of the Meunites, came against Jehoshaphat for battle.

2Men came and told Jehoshaphat, "A great multitude is coming against you from beyond the sea, from Aram. They are already in Hazazon-tamar," that is, En-gedi.

3Jehoshaphat was afraid, and he set his face to seek the LORD, and proclaimed a fast throughout all Judah.

4Judah gathered to seek help from the LORD; from all the cities of Judah they came to seek the LORD.

Jehoshaphat's Prayer

5Jehoshaphat stood in the assembly of Judah and Jerusalem, in the house of the LORD, before the new court,

6and said, "O LORD, God of our fathers, are You not God in heaven? You rule over all the kingdoms of the nations. In Your hand are power and might, so that none can stand against You.

7Did You not, our God, drive out the inhabitants of this land before Your people Israel, and give it forever to the seed of Abraham Your friend?

8They have lived in it and have built You a sanctuary in it for Your name, saying,

9'If evil comes on us, the sword of judgment, or plague, or famine, we will stand before this house and before You, for Your name is in this house, and cry out to You in our distress, and You will hear and save.'

10And now the sons of Ammon and Moab and Mount Seir, whom You would not let Israel invade when they came out of the land of Egypt, so that they turned aside from them and did not destroy them —

11they are repaying us by coming to drive us out of Your possession, which You gave us to possess.

12Our God, will You not judge them? For we have no power against this great multitude that is coming against us. We do not know what to do, but our eyes are on You."

13All Judah stood before the LORD, with their little ones, their wives and their sons.

Jahaziel's Word

14Then the Spirit of the LORD came on Jahaziel son of Zechariah, son of Benaiah, son of Jeiel, son of Mattaniah, the Levite, of the sons of Asaph, in the middle of the assembly.

15He said, "Listen, all Judah, inhabitants of Jerusalem and King Jehoshaphat. Thus says the LORD to you: Do not be afraid and do not lose heart because of this great multitude, for the battle is not yours but God's.

16Tomorrow go down against them. They will be coming up by the ascent of Ziz, and you will find them at the end of the valley, east of the wilderness of Jeruel.

17You will not need to fight in this battle. Take your positions, stand still and see the deliverance of the LORD with you, Judah and Jerusalem. Do not be afraid and do not lose heart. Tomorrow go out against them, and the LORD will be with you."

18Jehoshaphat bowed with his face to the ground, and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem fell down before the LORD, worshiping the LORD.

19The Levites, of the sons of the Kohathites and of the sons of the Korahites, stood up to praise the LORD, the God of Israel, with a very loud voice.

The Valley of Blessing

20They rose early in the morning and went out to the wilderness of Tekoa. As they went out, Jehoshaphat stood and said, "Hear me, Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem! Believe in the LORD your God, and you will be established; believe His prophets, and you will succeed."

21When he had taken counsel with the people, he appointed singers to the LORD to praise Him in holy splendor as they went out before the army, saying, "Give thanks to the LORD, for His loyal love endures forever."

22When they began to sing and praise, the LORD set ambushes against the sons of Ammon, Moab and Mount Seir who had come against Judah, and they were struck down.

23The sons of Ammon and Moab rose against the inhabitants of Mount Seir to devote them to destruction and wipe them out, and when they had finished with the inhabitants of Seir, they helped to destroy one another.

24When Judah came to the watchtower of the wilderness, they looked toward the multitude: they were dead bodies lying on the ground, and none had escaped.

25When Jehoshaphat and his people came to take their spoil, they found among them goods in abundance, corpses and precious things, more than they could carry away. They were three days taking the spoil, it was so much.

26On the fourth day they assembled in the Valley of Beracah, for there they blessed the LORD. That is why the name of that place is called the Valley of Beracah to this day.

27Then all the men of Judah and Jerusalem, with Jehoshaphat at their head, returned to Jerusalem with joy, for the LORD had made them rejoice over their enemies.

28They came to Jerusalem, to the house of the LORD, with harps, lyres and trumpets.

29The fear of God fell on all the kingdoms of the lands when they heard that the LORD had fought against the enemies of Israel.

30So the kingdom of Jehoshaphat was quiet, for his God gave him rest on every side.

The End of Jehoshaphat's Reign

31So Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah. He was thirty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Azubah the daughter of Shilhi.

32He walked in the way of Asa his father and did not turn aside from it, doing what was right in the eyes of the LORD.

33Yet the high places were not removed; the people had not yet set their hearts on the God of their fathers.

34The rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, from first to last, are written in the words of Jehu son of Hanani, which are entered in the book of the kings of Israel.

35After this Jehoshaphat king of Judah joined with Ahaziah king of Israel, who acted wickedly.

36He joined with him to make ships to go to Tarshish, and they made the ships in Ezion-geber.

37Then Eliezer son of Dodavahu of Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat, saying, "Because you have joined with Ahaziah, the LORD has broken down your works." The ships were wrecked and were not able to go to Tarshish.

Notes

  • v1 "some of the Meunites" — the Hebrew has me-ha-Ammonim, some of the Ammonites, after the sons of Ammon in the same sentence. The Greek has ek tōn Meinaiōn, of the Meunites, a people named again in Uzziah's wars (26:7), and the army is called Ammon, Moab and Mount Seir in vv10, 22–23. The text follows the Greek.

  • v2 "from Aram" — me-Aram, and the Greek agrees, from Syria. Edom, which differs by one letter, would fit an army that includes Mount Seir; no witness here has it. The text keeps the Hebrew.

  • v7 "the seed of Abraham Your friend" — ohavkha, who loved You, as the LORD calls him in Isaiah 41:8, the seed of Abraham, My friend. James takes it up: he was called the friend of God (James 2:23).

  • v9 "If evil comes on us… You will hear and save" — Solomon's prayer at the dedication (6:28–30), now prayed back.

  • v10 "whom You would not let Israel invade" — the LORD's word in the wilderness: I will not give you any of their land… because I have given Mount Seir to Esau (Deuteronomy 2:5), and the same for Moab and Ammon (2:9, 19).

  • vv15, 17 "the battle is not yours but God's… stand still and see the deliverance of the LORD" — David's words to Goliath, the battle is the LORD's (1 Samuel 17:47), and Moses' at the sea, Stand still and see the deliverance of the LORD (Exodus 14:13).

  • v20 "Believe… and you will be established" — ha'aminu… ve-te'amenu, the same verb twice: trust, and be made firm. Isaiah said it to Ahaz in the negative, If you will not believe, you will not be established (Isaiah 7:9).

  • v26 "the Valley of Beracah" — berakhah, blessing, named for what they did there: there they blessed the LORD.

  • vv35–37 "joined with Ahaziah… the ships were wrecked" — Kings: the ships were wrecked at Ezion-geber, and afterward Jehoshaphat would not let Ahaziah's men sail with his (1 Kings 22:48–49). Chronicles has the alliance come first and a prophet name it as the cause.
